name: leo_demo
description: Demo profile. One user, Maya, over about four months: an ICU nurse in Barcelona with a husband (Tomas), a daughter (Ines, 6), a Maine Coon cat (Mochi), a pescatarian diet, a cello in a community orchestra, and one preference for the answers of Leo: short, in bullet points. The preference goes with every message, and the facts only when they fit, so the demo shows both rules. The chats cover many topics, some with several turns on different subtopics, for the search of conversations. The user turns also hold things that must not be learned: a one-off state, a card number, a medicine, an order to the assistant, and task questions.

turns.user: My husband Tomas and I live in an old 1920s apartment in Barcelona. The bedroom walls smell musty and have dark patches near the floor. What causes that and how do we fix it?
turns.assistant:
Dark patches low on a wall in an old building are usually rising damp or condensation. Rising damp comes up from the ground through the masonry, leaves a tide mark up to about a metre high, and often salts the plaster so it crumbles. Condensation forms where warm, wet air meets a cold wall, mostly in corners and behind furniture, and it grows black mould.

To tell them apart, check whether the patches change with the weather and with how much you ventilate. A cheap hygrometer helps: indoor humidity above 65 percent points to condensation.

For condensation, ventilate every morning, keep furniture a few centimetres from outside walls and heat the room evenly. For rising damp, a surveyor should check the old damp-proof course; the usual fixes are an injected chemical barrier and lime plaster, which lets the wall breathe, instead of cement or gypsum, which trap the water.

turns.user: The electrician says the wiring is the original fabric covered cable. Do we really have to replace all of it?
turns.assistant:
Almost certainly yes. Fabric or rubber insulated cable from that period becomes brittle, and the insulation cracks when it is disturbed, which is a fire and shock risk. Old circuits also tend to have no earth wire and no residual current device.

A full rewire is messy because it means chasing channels into the walls, so do it before any plastering or painting. Use the chance to add sockets where you actually need them, a separate circuit for the kitchen and for an electric oven, and a modern consumer unit with RCD protection on every circuit.

Ask for a written quote that lists the number of circuits, the sockets and switches, and whether making good the plaster is included. Expect a two bedroom flat to take one to two weeks.

turns.user: The old cast iron radiators make a gurgling noise and are only warm at the bottom. Is something broken?
turns.assistant:
Probably not. A radiator that is cold at the top and warm at the bottom has trapped air, and the gurgling is that air moving around. The fix is to bleed it.

Turn the heating off and let the radiators cool. Hold a cloth under the bleed valve at the top corner, put a radiator key in the valve and turn it a quarter turn anticlockwise. You will hear a hiss as the air escapes. Close the valve as soon as water comes out.

After you bleed all of them, check the boiler pressure gauge. Bleeding lets some water out, so a sealed system may need topping up to about 1 to 1.5 bar. If a radiator is cold at the bottom instead, that is sludge, and the system needs a power flush. Old cast iron radiators are worth keeping: they hold heat for a long time.

turns.user: For the bathroom floor, should we pick porcelain or natural stone tiles?
turns.assistant:
For a bathroom floor, porcelain is the safer choice. It absorbs almost no water, does not need sealing, resists stains and comes in a matte or textured finish with good slip resistance. Many porcelain tiles now look very much like stone or wood.

Natural stone such as marble or limestone is beautiful and warm in character, but it is porous. It needs sealing when it is laid and again every year or two, it can etch with acidic cleaners, and polished stone gets slippery when wet.

Whichever you choose, ask for an R10 or R11 slip rating, plan the falls towards the drain, and use a flexible tile adhesive, because old timber floors move. Underfloor heating works well under both.

chats.title: Cleaning a messy CSV with pandas

turns.user: I'm an ICU nurse. A CSV export of our shift schedules has dates in different formats and some duplicated rows. How do I clean it with pandas?
turns.assistant:
Read the file with everything as text first, so pandas does not guess wrong types: df = pd.read_csv('shifts.csv', dtype=str).

For mixed date formats, use pd.to_datetime(df['date'], format='mixed', dayfirst=True, errors='coerce'). Rows that cannot be parsed become NaT, so you can list them with df[df['date'].isna()] and fix them by hand.

To remove duplicates, decide which columns define a duplicate. For shifts it is probably the person, the date and the start time: df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['name', 'date', 'start']). Strip spaces and normalise case first, for example df['name'] = df['name'].str.strip().str.title(), or near duplicates will survive.

Finally sort and save: df.sort_values(['date', 'start']).to_csv('clean.csv', index=False).

turns.user: Now I want the total hours per person per month, and night shifts counted separately.
turns.assistant:
Build start and end datetimes, then the length of each shift. A night shift ends after midnight, so add a day when the end is before the start:

start = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['start'])
end = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['end'])
end = end.where(end > start, end + pd.Timedelta(days=1))
df['hours'] = (end - start).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

Mark a shift as a night shift when it starts at 20:00 or later: df['night'] = start.dt.hour >= 20.

Then group by person and month: df['month'] = start.dt.to_period('M'), and summary = df.pivot_table(index=['name', 'month'], columns='night', values='hours', aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0). Rename the columns to day and night hours, and you have one row per person and month.

turns.user: My home espresso machine drips water from around the group head when I pull a shot. Is it broken?
turns.assistant:
Water around the group head while brewing almost always means a worn group gasket, the rubber ring that the portafilter presses against. Over time it hardens and stops sealing, so pressurised water escapes around the edge.

First check the easy things: clean coffee grounds off the gasket and the portafilter rim, and make sure you are not overfilling the basket, which stops the portafilter from locking fully.

If it still leaks, replace the gasket and the shower screen together. They are cheap and specific to your model. Unscrew the shower screen, prise the old gasket out with a small screwdriver, clean the groove, and push the new one in evenly. Most people need to do this every one to two years.

turns.user: How often should I descale it, and is vinegar fine?
turns.assistant:
It depends on your water. With hard water, descale every one to two months; with soft or filtered water, every three to four months. White crust around the steam wand or a slower flow are signs it is due.

Avoid vinegar. It is hard to rinse out, leaves a taste, and the acetic acid can damage rubber seals and some metals. Use a citric acid or lactic acid descaler made for espresso machines, at the strength on the pack.

Run the solution through the group head and the steam wand in small amounts, let it sit for about twenty minutes, then flush with at least two full tanks of fresh water. If your machine has a boiler with a brass or aluminium part, check the manual, because some makers name the descaler you should use.

turns.user: That was a lot to read. I prefer short answers in bullet points.
turns.assistant:

turns.user: How should ten days in Japan be split between Tokyo and Kyoto?
turns.assistant:
Ten days fits well as four days in Tokyo, four in Kyoto, and two for a day trip and travel. Start in Tokyo to get over the jet lag in a city where everything is open late.

In Tokyo, group the sights by area: Asakusa and Ueno on one day, Shibuya, Harajuku and Shinjuku on another, and a calm day in Yanaka or a trip to Kamakura. In Kyoto, start very early at Fushimi Inari and Kiyomizu-dera, before the crowds, and leave one day for Arashiyama and its bamboo grove.

From Kyoto, Nara is an easy half day, and Osaka is good for an evening of street food. Spring is cherry blossom season, so book hotels several months ahead.

turns.user: We want to try a traditional hot spring. What are the rules there?
turns.assistant:
Onsen etiquette is simple but strict. You bathe naked, and baths are usually split by gender. Swimsuits are not allowed.

Before you get into the bath, wash your whole body at the shower stations, sitting on the small stool, and rinse off all the soap. The bath is for soaking, not for washing.

You get a small towel: do not put it in the water. People fold it and put it on their head or at the edge. Tie long hair up so it does not touch the water. Keep your voice low and do not swim or splash.

Many onsen still refuse people with tattoos. Some accept them if they are covered with a patch, and private family baths, called kashikiri, are a good choice if you are not sure.

turns.user: Is the JR Pass still worth it?
turns.assistant:
Since the big price increase in 2023, the national JR Pass is worth it only if you travel a lot. For a Tokyo and Kyoto trip with one return Shinkansen and some local trains, single tickets are usually cheaper.

Add up your planned long trips on a fare calculator before you decide. A Tokyo to Kyoto Shinkansen ticket is about 14,000 yen one way, so a return is far below the price of a seven day pass.

For city travel, get a Suica or Pasmo card in a phone wallet. It works on trains, subways and buses and in many shops. Regional passes, such as the Kansai area pass, can still pay off for several day trips from Kyoto.

turns.user: The tomato plants on our balcony have brown spots with yellow rings on the lower leaves, and they are spreading up. What is it?
turns.assistant:
Brown spots with yellow rings, starting on the lowest leaves, sound like early blight, a fungal disease. The spots often have rings inside them like a target. Late blight looks different: large grey-green, greasy patches that spread very fast in wet weather, often with white fuzz under the leaf.

For early blight, remove the affected leaves at once and put them in the bin, not in compost. Water the soil, not the leaves, and in the morning, so the plant dries during the day. Mulch the soil so splashing water does not carry the spores up.

Give the plants more space and air, and cut the lowest leaves so none touch the soil. A copper based fungicide can slow it down. Next year, use fresh compost in the pots and pick resistant varieties.

turns.user: We are choosing between a fixed rate and a variable rate mortgage. How do we decide?
turns.assistant:
A fixed rate gives you the same payment for the fixed period, so you can plan your budget and you are protected if rates rise. It usually starts a little higher, and leaving the deal early can cost a penalty.

A variable rate follows a reference rate, in Europe usually Euribor, plus a fixed spread. It is often cheaper at the start and you gain when rates fall, but your payment can go up a lot when they rise.

Ask yourselves how much a payment rise would hurt. A useful test is to work out the payment if the rate went up by two or three points. If that would be a real problem, fix. Many people choose a mixed loan: fixed for the first years, variable after. Compare the total cost, called the APR or TAEG, not just the headline rate.

turns.user: I play the cello in a community orchestra. How can I practice well in only twenty minutes a day?
turns.assistant:
Twenty focused minutes a day beats two hours once a week. Split the time into three parts.

Spend five minutes on long, slow bows on open strings and a scale, listening for an even tone from the frog to the tip. Then spend ten minutes on the hardest passage of the orchestra piece: a few bars at a slow tempo with a metronome, raising the speed only when it is clean twice in a row. Finish with five minutes of playing something you enjoy, all the way through.

Keep the cello out of its case on a stand, so starting takes seconds. A short note after each session about what to work on next saves time at the start of the following one.

turns.user: My shifting in the second movement is always out of tune. Any tips?
turns.assistant:
Out of tune shifts usually come from moving the whole arm too late and too fast. Practise the shift slowly with a guide note: keep the finger that is on the string lightly in contact and slide it to its new place, so you hear the distance, then put down the target finger.

Think of the shift as an arm movement led from the elbow, not as a jump of the hand. Keep the thumb relaxed behind the neck so it travels with the hand.

Check the arrival note against an open string where you can, for example a D against the open D string, and listen for the ring. When the slow version is reliable, make the audible slide smaller and quicker until it disappears.

turns.user: We have a six-year-old daughter, Ines. She woke up at night with a fever of 38.7. When should we worry?
turns.assistant:
A fever of 38.7 in a six year old is common with viral infections and is not dangerous by itself. What matters most is how she looks and behaves.

You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose for her weight if she is uncomfortable, offer small drinks often, and dress her lightly. Fever reducers are for comfort, not to reach a normal number.

Call a doctor or an emergency line at once if she is hard to wake, very floppy, breathing fast or with effort, has a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when you press a glass on it, signs of dehydration such as no urine for many hours, or a seizure. See a doctor within a day if the fever lasts more than three days, comes with ear pain or pain when peeing, or if your instinct says something is wrong.

turns.user: My half marathon is in two weeks. How should I reduce my training before the race?
turns.assistant:
A two week taper is right for a half marathon. The goal is to arrive rested without losing fitness, so you cut the volume but keep some intensity.

In the first week, run about 70 to 80 percent of your usual distance, with one shorter session at race pace, for example three times two kilometres. In race week, drop to about half, with two or three short easy runs and a few strides, and rest completely the day before or do a very short jog.

Do not try anything new: no new shoes, no new gels, no hard gym sessions. Sleep matters more than any extra run. It is normal to feel sluggish or restless during a taper; it does not mean you lost fitness.

turns.user: What should I eat the night before and the morning of the race?
turns.assistant:
The night before, eat a normal sized meal that is rich in carbohydrates and that you know well, such as rice, pasta or potatoes with a simple sauce. Keep fat, fibre and spice moderate, and do not overeat: carbohydrate loading matters more for a full marathon.

On the morning, eat two to three hours before the start: toast with honey or jam, a banana, or oats. Drink a glass or two of water, and a coffee if you usually have one.

For a half marathon, many runners take one gel around kilometre 12 to 14. Practise this in a long training run first, so your stomach is used to it. Drink at the water stations when you are thirsty, but do not force large amounts.

turns.user: How do I start shooting film on an old Pentax K1000?
turns.assistant:
The K1000 is a great camera to restart with: fully mechanical, so it works without a battery, except for the light meter.

First check the basics. Put a fresh LR44 or SR44 battery in for the meter, open the back and look for torn light seals or crumbly foam, and fire the shutter at all speeds with the back open to hear that the slow speeds really are slower.

Load a forgiving film such as Kodak Gold 200 or Portra 400, which handle over exposure well. Set the ISO on the dial, and use the needle in the viewfinder: centre it with the aperture and shutter speed. In doubt, give more light rather than less. Shoot one roll, get it developed and scanned at a local lab, and you will know if the camera needs repair.

turns.user: The photos came back with a light orange streak on the edge. What happened?
turns.assistant:
An orange or red streak along the edge of the frames is a light leak. Colour negative film turns orange where stray light reaches it.

The usual cause is old light seals. The foam strips in the channels around the back door and the hinge turn sticky or fall apart, and light gets in. Look where the streak is: at the hinge side or along the top and bottom of every frame points to the door seals.

Replacing the seals is a cheap home job: kits for the K1000 cost a few euros. Remove the old foam with a wooden toothpick and some lighter fluid, clean the channels, and press in the new strips. A leak only on the first frames of the roll is normal, from loading the film in daylight.

turns.user: We have a Maine Coon named Mochi. How do we keep a cat from scratching a new sofa?
turns.assistant:
Scratching is normal for a cat: it keeps the claws healthy, stretches the back and leaves her scent. The goal is not to stop it but to move it to something she likes more than the sofa.

A Maine Coon is big, so she needs a tall, heavy scratching post that does not wobble, at least 80 centimetres high, covered in sisal rope. Put it right next to the sofa, where she already scratches, and add a flat cardboard scratcher too: some cats prefer to scratch lying down.

Make the sofa less attractive for a few weeks with double-sided tape or a throw over the arms. Reward her with a treat or play every time she uses the post, and rub a little catnip or silvervine on it. Trim her claws every two weeks. Never punish her: it makes her scratch when you are not there.

turns.user: How do we stop a cat from meowing for food at five in the morning?
turns.assistant:
Early waking is a habit she learned: meowing at five brought breakfast. To break it, the food has to stop coming from you at that hour.

An automatic feeder works best. Set it to give a small meal at five, so the food comes from the machine, not from the bed. Move her biggest meal to late in the evening, after a long play session with a wand toy, so she goes to sleep tired and full.

Do not get up, talk to her or push her away when she meows: any reaction is a reward. It will get worse for a few days before it gets better. If the meowing starts suddenly in an older cat, see a vet, because thyroid problems and pain can cause it.

turns.user: I'm pescatarian. Can you give me a meal prep plan for three work lunches?
turns.assistant:
Here is a plan you can cook in about an hour on a day off, for three lunches that keep well.

First, a tray of roasted chickpeas, sweet potato and red onion with smoked paprika. Second, a pot of brown rice or farro. Third, baked salmon fillets with lemon and dill, or a tin of good sardines kept for the third day.

Lunch one: rice, salmon, roasted vegetables and a yoghurt and herb sauce. Lunch two: a salad of farro, chickpeas, cucumber, feta and olives, which gets better after a day. Lunch three: a tuna and white bean salad with parsley and lemon.

Keep the sauces in small separate jars, so nothing goes soggy. Cooked fish keeps two to three days in the fridge, so eat the salmon first.

turns.user: My card 4539 1488 0343 6467 was declined at the pharmacy when I bought my sertraline. Why would that happen?
turns.assistant:
A card can be declined for several reasons that have nothing to do with the shop: not enough funds, a daily limit, an expired card, a wrong PIN, or a fraud check by the bank that blocks an unusual payment.

Check your banking app first. It often shows the declined payment and the reason, and it may ask you to confirm that the payment was yours. If the app shows nothing, call the number on the back of the card.

Please do not share your full card number in chats or emails. If you think it may have been seen by others, ask your bank to block the card and send a new one.

turns.assistant: I can answer in Catalan whenever you write to me in Catalan or ask for it in a chat. I will still be clear that I am an AI assistant when that matters.

turns.user: I'm on four night shifts in a row this week. How do I sleep during the day?
turns.assistant:
Treat your day sleep like night sleep. Make the room very dark with blackout curtains or a sleep mask, cool, and quiet, with earplugs or white noise. Put the phone on do not disturb.

On the way home in the morning, wear sunglasses so the bright light does not wake your body clock. Go to bed soon after you get home, and aim for one long block of sleep. A short nap of about 90 minutes before the first night shift helps too.

Avoid caffeine in the last four to six hours of your shift, eat a light meal before sleeping rather than a heavy one, and keep the same routine on all four days.
